title: Γυνὴ μάγος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 91 (= Perry 56). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Γυνὴ μάγος ἐπῳδὰς καὶ θείων καταθέσεις μηνιμάτων ἐπαγγελλομένη διετέλει πολλὰ τελοῦσα καὶ ἐκ τούτων οὐ μικρὰ βιοποριστοῦσα.
sentences.tr: Gynē magos epōidas kai theiōn katatheseis mēnimatōn epangellomenē dietelei polla telousa kai ek toutōn ou mikra bioporistousa.
sentences.l: A woman sorcerer, professing charms and the laying-to-rest of divine wraths, continued performing many rites and from these making no small living.
sentences.i: A sorceress who advertised spells and the laying of divine wrath went on performing all manner of rites and making no small living out of them.
sentences.n: διατελέω with supplementary participles again (τελοῦσα, βιοποριστοῦσα): the verb gives the duration, the participles the action. τελέω is the verb for performing rites — the τελεταί, initiations, stand behind it. οὐ μικρά is litotes: she did very well indeed. The genitive θείων … μηνιμάτων is split around its noun, an elevated arrangement that suits her professional patter.

sentences.t: Ἐπὶ τούτοις ἐγγραφόμενοί τινες αὐτὴν ὡς καινοτομοῦσαν περὶ τὰ θεῖα, εἰς δίκην ἀπήγαγον καὶ κατηγορήσαντες κατεδίκασαν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ θανάτῳ.
sentences.tr: Epi toutois engraphomenoi tines autēn hōs kainotomousan peri ta theia, eis dikēn apēgagon kai katēgorēsantes katedikasan autēn epi thanatōi.
sentences.l: On these grounds certain men, entering an indictment against her as innovating in what concerns the gods, led her off to trial and, having accused her, condemned her to death.
sentences.i: On these grounds certain men indicted her for religious innovation, brought her to trial, prosecuted her, and had her sentenced to death.
sentences.n: ὡς with a participle gives the ground as the accusers allege it, not as the narrator asserts it. καινοτομεῖν περὶ τὰ θεῖα, 'to innovate in matters of religion', stands very close to the Athenian charge of ἀσέβεια on which Socrates was tried. ἐπὶ θανάτῳ, 'with death as the penalty'. κατεδίκασαν keeps the accusers as its subject where English wants the court: in Greek the prosecutors are made the agents of the whole outcome, sentence included.

sentences.t: Θεασάμενος δέ τις αὐτὴν ἀπαγομένην ἐκ τῶν δικαστηρίων ἔφη· « Ὦ αὕτη, ἡ τὰς δαιμόνων ὀργὰς ἀποτρέπειν ἐπαγγελλομένη, πῶς οὐδὲ ἀνθρώπους πεῖσαι ἠδυνήθης ; »
sentences.tr: Theasamenos de tis autēn apagomenēn ek tōn dikastēriōn ephē· « Ō hautē, hē tas daimonōn orgas apotrepein epangellomenē, pōs oude anthrōpous peisai ēdynēthēs ; »
sentences.l: And someone, having seen her led away from the courts, said: « You there, who profess to turn aside the angers of divinities — how were you not able to persuade even men? »
sentences.i: And someone who saw her being led away from the courts said: « You there — you who advertise that you can turn aside the anger of the divinities: how is it you could not talk round even men? »
sentences.n: Ὦ αὕτη puts the nominative where a vocative would stand, 'you there, woman' — brusque, not respectful. The joke turns on the two audiences, δαίμονες above and mere ἄνθρωποι, the jurors, below; οὐδέ, 'not even', is the sting.

sentences.t: Τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ χρήσαιτο ἄν τις πρὸς γυναῖκα πλάνον, ἥτις τὰ μείζονα κατεπαγγελλομένη τοῖς μετρίοις ἀδύνατος ἐλέγχεται.
sentences.tr: Toutōi tōi logōi chrēsaito an tis pros gynaika planon, hētis ta meizona katepangellomenē tois metriois adynatos elenchetai.
sentences.l: This story someone might use against a charlatan woman, who, undertaking the greater things, is convicted of being powerless in ordinary ones.
sentences.n: χρήσαιτο ἄν is the potential optative, 'someone might use' — the cautious mood these applications habitually take. πλάνος is the wanderer, hence the vagabond quack. ἐλέγχεται keeps the courtroom sense of ἔλεγχος: she is convicted, and of incapacity. τὰ μείζονα against τοῖς μετρίοις sets the two scales side by side.
